title: Jain Khan Urges Abdali to Strike the Fighting Singhs First

blocks.text: Abdali rebukes Jain Khan for failing to stop the Sikhs even though he commands a large mounted force and has support from Malerkotla and other allies. The rebuke carries a clear political sting: if such strength cannot hold the Khalsa at the front, then Jain Khan's earlier confidence means little.

Jain Khan launches another attempt, but Sham Singh's men throw it back and prove again that a frontal check will not come easily. He returns from the field admitting that it is better to attack the Singhs instead of invading the caravan, because the armed jathas are the shield that keeps the rest of the column alive.

Abdali accepts that logic and shifts the pressure toward the fighting Sikhs themselves. The Singhs respond by giving ground only while firing and cutting back at the pursuers, keeping the retreat disciplined even under overwhelming force.
